newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech blue chips rebound, lead PX50 index higher.
newsitem.headline: Czech blue chips rebound, lead PX50 index higher.

text.p: Czech blue chip shares rebounded on the Prague Stock Exchange on Tuesday, while broader issues also gained ground as the official PX50 index closed 2.7 points, or 0.50 percent higher at 540.5.
Some high cap issues were hit hard in early trading this week, the result of a sharp drop on Wall Street at the end of last week.
But SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- which account for nearly one half of the index's capitalisation -- all bounced back on Tuesday.
Total volume, boosted mainly by direct and block trades, was lighter at 443,887 shares on turnover of 698 million crowns. Overall, 104 shares closed higher, 86 were lower and 53 held steady.
Radio transmission company Ceske Radiokomunikace continued to post solid gains with a 51 crown, 1.1 percent, rise to 4,651.
The company has surged since TeleDanmark announced a week ago that it had taken a 20.8 percent stake in the company.
While the news was welcomed as positive for Radiokomunikace, analysts have noted that the free float in the company is now extremely low, making it less attractive.

"Although we feel this is a positive development for Radiokomunikace, TeleDanmark's purchase has lowered the already unimpressive free float to an estimated 5.8 percent, Eugene Klerk of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said.
"With (this)...we downgrade the stock from buy to hold," he added.
